rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a comprehensive multimodal setup to establish baseline performance. This configuration tests multiprofile multimodal modeling with advanced RNA (scvi_n200) and image (imagenet_vit_l) encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion - key design choices that could significantly impact performance. It isolates the effect of sophisticated multimodal integration strategies while maintaining a balanced complexity level.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.725 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and directly compares against the current best. This balances exploration (testing a different fusion method) and exploitation (building on the existing multiprofile/multimodal setup).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_001) outperform concat fusion (config_003) by a small margin. This experiment tests the impact of replacing the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while keeping other parameters (multimodal, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) consistent. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision with potential to significantly influence performance. It balances exploration of key components with minimal changes to the proven baseline.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_001) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). However, the impact of RNA encoder choice (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) remains uncertain. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with the same image encoder and aggregation/fusion settings, isolating the effect of RNA representation. It directly addresses a key design choice with minimal parameter changes, providing clarity on whether RNA encoder selection significantly impacts performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders (config_001) achieve the highest accuracy. However, config_015 (resnet50 image encoder) has a higher F1, suggesting encoder choice matters. This experiment tests scgpt RNA + resnet50 image encoders (untested combination) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (similar to config_001), isolating the impact of encoder choices while maintaining proven aggregation/fusion strategies. It balances exploration of key design choices with exploitation of prior success.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method (from transformer to avgpool) while keeping RNA and image encoders the same impacts performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation, a critical design choice, and clarifies whether the current aggregation method is optimal. This balances exploitation of the best-performing components with exploration of key hyperparameters.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy. Uncertainty remains about whether the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) or fusion method (concat vs weighted) significantly impacts performance. Testing config_023 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) isolates these factors while maintaining other top-performing parameters. This comparison clarifies the relative importance of image encoder choice and fusion strategy, balancing exploration of critical design decisions with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (while keeping other parameters identical) impacts performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. This is critical to determine if scvi_n200 is essential or if simpler encoders could suffice, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing aggregation to avgpool and fusion to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders the same) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation and fusion methods, which are critical design choices. Since config_001 is the top performer, this comparison will clarify if these components are key to its success, balancing exploration and exploitation efficiently.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile configurations with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_001: 0.725). This experiment tests the impact of switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping the image encoder, aggregation (transformer), and fusion (concat) consistent. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which is critical for understanding performance differences, even though scgpt has lower prior performance. It balances exploration of key design choices without overcomplicating the experiment.
